confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion, including Appendices A-D, and checked the recorded numbers against the PDF. The source is arXiv:2604.24444v1 dated 27 Apr 2026, with 29 PDF pages; the title and six named authors match the form (PDF p. 1; Appendices A-D, pp. 13-29; PDF page count).

S1 is a randomized within-person online study: the paper explicitly describes two randomized writing task blocks and random allocation of selected tasks between treatment and control. This supports online_rct and has_randomized_people_study=true; no more detailed block-order randomization procedure is stated (PDF p. 4, Section 4 and Figure 1; p. 24, Table 9 caption).

S1 recruited 100 people and analyzed 81 English-fluent Prolific participants. Responses were discarded if participants never edited any LLM draft or did not complete the study. A separate count at randomization is not reported, so n_randomized=null is appropriate; the analyzed sample exceeds the 50-person threshold (PDF pp. 4 and 13, Section 4 and Appendix A.1).

The same 81 analyzed people contributed to both conditions: each selected six of eight tasks, with four randomly assigned to AI-assisted post-editing and two to unassisted writing. The two arm counts must not be added as separate samples; Table 9 counts task observations, while the H2a outcome compares text pairs and has no stated total pair count (PDF p. 24, Table 9 and caption; p. 7, Figure 6).

GPT-o4-mini generated initial drafts from the writing-task type and participant-written planned details; participants then edited for personal style. Control writing was produced directly from plans without seeing LLM text, and participants were instructed to invent details (PDF pp. 4-5, Section 4, footnote 8, Prompt 4.1 and Section 5.1; p. 24, Appendix D).

The listed writing scenarios match Table 9. The minimum post-editing duration was two minutes per task, and mean main-study completion time was 1.69 hours (PDF p. 5, Section 4; p. 13, Appendix A.1; p. 24, Table 9).

H2a is diversity scored on produced output: cosine similarity of LUAR-MUD style embeddings compares writing from different participants. The form correctly uses diversity, across_people, embedding_similarity and pair; higher similarity means lower stylistic diversity (PDF p. 5, Section 5.2; pp. 6-7, Section 6.2 and Figure 6; p. 16, Appendix B.2 and Table 3).

The sole reported contrast and the one-line finding reproduce the printed H2a result exactly: p = .0002, Hedges g = 1.42, 95% CI [1.33, 1.51], comparing post-edited writing with unassisted human writing. Retaining the printed positive sign while explaining that it denotes greater homogeneity is accurate (PDF p. 6, Section 6.2; p. 16, Table 3, H2a LUAR-MUD row).

The paper reports raw p-values, two-tailed permutation tests with 10,000 permutations, and 95% confidence intervals from 1000 bootstrap samples. It does not specify a participant-level bootstrap for H2a; the reported interval should not be described as participant-clustered precision (PDF p. 5, Section 6; pp. 13-14, Appendix A.2).

S2 is a separate formative task-selection survey, appropriately classified other: 102 respondents completed it and 88 passed attention checks; its respondents could not also complete the main study. Randomized scenario presentation is not randomized AI assistance, and the survey produced no scored creative-writing output (PDF pp. 22-23, Appendix C and Figure 14).

The formative survey presented fifteen candidate scenarios plus two attention checks, requested six actual tasks plus both checks, and had a median completion time of 3.53 minutes (PDF pp. 22-23, Appendix C).

The paper contains a qualifying randomized people study, rather than an observational or AI-versus-human-only context study; context_class=none is appropriate. It is not a synthesis, so no pooled estimates or synthesis study counts apply (PDF pp. 4-7, Sections 4-6; pp. 22-24, Appendices C-D).

The short-screening brief explicitly requires core=unclear for promotion to the two-screener pipeline and leaves unrequested fields at defaults. Preregistration, data availability and Pangram API credits are actually stated in the paper, but their corresponding default fields were outside that short-form extraction scope and are not corrections to the populated screening results (codex-jobs/lscreen-c710/brief.md, SHORT-form instructions and final paragraph; PDF p. 1, abstract and footnotes 2 and 4; p. 10, Acknowledgments).
summary: The recorded design, participant counts, source version, and H2a statistics match the PDF. The randomized within-person study analyzed 81 people and belongs in the two-screener pipeline.
